column1: # gentoo-install — Portage profile catalogue
# One record per (flavour, init) pair of data/stages.tsv. The flavour column
# here and the flavour column there are the same vocabulary on purpose: the
# stage3 you unpack and the profile you select have to agree, and a table that
# uses two different names for the same thing is how they stop agreeing.
# The profile column holds the exact name `eselect profile set` takes, which is
# also the path under <repo>/profiles. The installer never sets it on trust:
# it checks that the directory exists in the synced tree first, then walks the
# fallbacks column in order, and only then reports that nothing matches. An
# `eselect profile set` that fails is a bad error message ("invalid profile")
# on a machine that is three steps into an install; a directory test costs
# nothing and can name every candidate it tried.
# fallbacks is a comma-separated list of older names, tried left to right. The
# 23.0 profiles were introduced in 2023 and the 17.x ones outlived them by a
# while in real trees; a snapshot from before the switch still installs.
# status repeats what <repo>/profiles/profiles.desc says about the profile:
#   stable   supported, the arch team keeps it working
#   dev      usable, moves faster than stable
#   exp      experimental upstream, and the installer says so out loud
# use holds the USE flags gentoo-install adds to make.conf for that
# combination, or - for none. Most rows are -, and that is the point: the
# profile already carries the distribution's opinion, USE in make.conf is a
# delta on top of it, and an installer that fills that delta with its author's
# taste is an installer nobody else can use (DESIGN.md §15). The two rows that
# are not - fix something the profile genuinely leaves undone: an OpenRC
# desktop has no seat management without elogind, and a systemd desktop must
# not pull it in beside logind.
# The desktop flavour selects the plain desktop profile. The DE-specific ones
# (default/linux/amd64/23.0/desktop/gnome, .../desktop/plasma, and their
# systemd variants) are a choice this table does not make for you; name one
# through the configuration to override everything below:
#     portage_profile = default/linux/amd64/23.0/desktop/plasma/systemd
